sources.title: Florida Statutes s. 400.0255, Resident transfer or discharge; requirements and procedures; hearings
sources.notes: Matches the standing packet's own method, 'tag strip over the statute's Section div, ending at the History line': div#statutes holds exactly the section heading through the History line and excludes the search box and site chrome around it. Plain curl with a browser user-agent returns 200; no WAF sits in front of Online Sunshine, consistent with CLAUDE.md's note that leg.state.fl.us is curl-able with a browser user-agent. Typographic quotation marks and apostrophes are the publisher's own and are left untouched.

sources.title: Florida Department of Children and Families, Office of Inspector General — Appeal Hearings
sources.notes: The standing packet says this host 'refuses or defeats plain curl' and was captured through a session fetch tool; retested 2026-09-03, plain curl with a browser user-agent now returns 200 with the full page, including the hearing office's address (2415 North Monroe Street), phone (850) 488-1429 and the 'individual or family“s eligibility' string the standing packet quotes verbatim. Whatever blocked it on 2026-08-30 no longer does, or never did with this header. The page's own <main id="main-content"> element is empty in the served markup — the card content the page displays sits directly in <body>, several containers below main — so 'body' is the narrowest scope that is honestly stated and complete; it is also a superset of the standing packet's hand-curated excerpt, which the recipe README treats as safe.

sources.title: Florida Department of Elder Affairs, Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
sources.notes: Also recorded in the standing packet as defeating plain curl and captured through a session reader; retested 2026-09-03, plain curl with a browser user-agent returns 200 with the full Divi-theme page (the '14 district offices' line, the toll-free ombudsman number 1-888-831-0404, the Winewood Boulevard address and the 'medical reasons, the welfare of other residents or nonpayment of a bill' rights language all present). The page carries about 331 KB of markup but only ~16.6 KB of body text once script/style nodes are dropped, so 'body' is not the wide net it looks like; the resident-rights accordion content sits well outside any <main> or <article> wrapper this template exposes, so body is the narrowest honestly-stated scope, and again a safe superset of the standing packet's curated excerpt.

sources.title: Florida Administrative Code Chapter 65-2, Rules of Practice and Procedure (Department of Children and Families)
sources.source_date: most sections effective 4/2/2018 (per each rule's own History line on flrules.org; 65-2.058 effective 12/11/2006 and 65-2.060 effective 10/30/2000 are not amended by the 2018 rulemaking)
sources.notes: Captured to resolve the department's fair-hearing procedural rule that s. 400.0255(15)(b) points to ('equivalent to the procedures used for fair hearings for other Medicaid cases, chapter 10-2, part VI, Florida Administrative Code'): each rule in the current chapter carries a History line reading 'Formerly 10-2.xx, 10-2.0xx', so chapter 65-2 is chapter 10-2 under its current number, though the current chapter prints no 'Part' subdivisions and this page cannot confirm which rules made up 'Part VI' specifically -- recorded as a finding, not resolved. flrules.org (Florida's official Administrative Code publisher) serves this chapter's full current text only as a single legacy binary Word file (Composite Document Format / 'Word 6.0/95', per the `file` command), not as a .docx, PDF, or HTML rendering -- checked: the chapter's own listing page offers no other format, and every individual rule's own readFile.asp link is the same legacy .doc. The docx extractor reads that format as of 2026-09-05: capture.py sniffs the Composite Document Format header and converts with textutil rather than python-docx, which reads only the OOXML zip container (FA-Q-20260905-01). The converter is an input to the captured text in the same way the pinned poppler build is, and capture.py names the one that ran on stderr -- this source's text was produced by textutil. Until that landed, the file was fetched by curl and converted outside the tool with `textutil -convert txt`, then handed in with `--supply 5=<file>`; that workaround is retired and this source now captures unattended.

sources.title: Florida Medicaid Nursing Facility Services Coverage Policy, Rule 59G-4.200, F.A.C. (Agency for Health Care Administration)
sources.notes: Found from ahca.myflorida.com's own 'Adopted Rules and Service Specific Policies' listing page (medicaid/rules/adopted-rules-service-specific-policies.html), which links this PDF as '59G-4.200 Nursing Facility Services Coverage Policy'; the document's own section 1.2 states its legal authority as 'Rule 59G-4.200, F.A.C.' among others. This is AHCA's own first-party statement of the Medicaid bed-hold ('leave days') policy the licensure statute (400.0255(6), 400.022(1)(u)) refers to without stating a Medicaid-specific day count of its own: section 4.2.1, 'Leave Days', states 'Florida Medicaid reimburses for leave days when the recipient is expected to return to the facility, as follows: Hospitalization -- 8 days per medically necessary hospital stay; Therapeutic leave -- 16 days per state fiscal year.' This 8-day figure differs from 400.022(1)(u)'s own 'up to 15 days' for a Title XIX (Medicaid) resident's hospitalization bed reservation; both are quoted on the page as published by their own publishers and are not reconciled. Single-column PDF, seven pages, no WAF encountered; plain curl with a browser user-agent returns 200 directly.
